en: The Apadāna of the Elder Bākula Pilindavaccha Chapter 6 I was a young brahmin, well-versed in the Vedas, And I had mastered the three Vedas along with their ancillaries. Then, having heard of the Buddha, the peerless man, I went to the presence of the Teacher. Having approached the Sugata, I spoke these words: "O Great Hero, I am a seeker of the Dhamma; Please teach me the Dhamma, O Knower of the World. Then the Teacher taught me the Dhamma. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. With a heart full of joy, I took refuge In the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha. Then, having paid homage to the Teacher, I departed from his presence. At that time, I was a householder, Possessing great wealth and abundance. I gave alms-food to the Saṅgha, Led by the Buddha, the Great Sage. For eighty-four thousand years, I offered food to the Saṅgha. When the Teacher passed away into Nibbāna, I built a stūpa for the relics. It was made of gold and silver, Adorned with jewels and pearls. I honored it with perfumes and garlands, And with various kinds of incense. By this root of merit, I have attained the state of an Arhat. Now, having seen the Buddha, the peerless man, I have reached the end of suffering. This is my final birth; There will be no further existence. Thus did the Elder Bākula speak Of his own former deeds. Having heard this, one should reflect: "May I too become like him!"
Not far from the Himālaya is a mountain named Sobhita;
there my well-constructed hermitage stands.
It was built by his own disciples.
And there were many pavilions there,
with blooming sinduvāra trees.
And there were many kapittha trees in full bloom, as well as many jīvajīvaka trees;
there were also many nigguṇḍī trees there.
And jujubes and emblic myrobalans;
phārusaka fruits and gourds,
and blooming white lotuses.
There are Āḷaka beluva trees there,
as well as plantains and mātuluṅga trees;
many mahānāma trees are there too.
The *ajjuna*, *piyaṅguka*,
*kosamba*, *saḷala*, *nimba*,
*nigrodha*, and *kapittha* trees;
That was my hermitage;
I lived there with my disciples.
The Blessed One Anomadassī—
The Self-Existent One, the Leader of the World,
seeking seclusion,
came to my hermitage.
When the Great Hero Anomadassi of great glory had arrived,
in an instant, [I saw] the Lord of the World.
An affliction by wind arose.
While wandering in the forest,
I saw the Leader of the World.
Having approached the Fully Awakened One,
the Visionary of Great Renown,
and having observed his deportment as well,
I observed that at that time,
without a doubt, illness had arisen for the Buddha.
I quickly returned to the hermitage,
in the presence of my disciples,
desiring to prepare a medicinal remedy.
I then addressed my disciples.
Having responded to my words with respect, all my disciples—
endowed with reverence— [listened].
They gathered together all at once out of reverence for my Teacher;
quickly ascending the mountain, they stood there.
Having prepared a mixture of water,
I gave it to the Best of Buddhas, who is capable of enduring all poisons.
When the Great Hero,
the omniscient leader of the world, had finished his meal,
the wind quickly subsided.
Of the Sugata, the Great Seer.
Seeing his agitation stilled,
Anomadassin, of great renown, [spoke].
Having sat down on his own seat,
he spoke these verses:
“He who gave me medicine...”
And my own illness, O observer of the observance day;
that I shall proclaim,
listen as I speak.
For a hundred thousand eons,
he will delight in the world of the gods,
there amidst the sounding of musical instruments.
This one shall always rejoice.
Having come to the world of humans,
impelled by the root of merit;
A thousand times he will be a wheel-turning monarch;
in the fifty-fifth aeon, [he will become a Buddha].
A kshatriya named Anoma,
victorious on all four sides,
lord of the Jambudvīpa realm.
Endowed with the seven treasures,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power,
having even shaken the realm of the Thirty-three,
He will exercise lordship.
Whether as a god or a human,
he will be free from illness.
Having avoided grasping,
one will cross over the disease in the world.
In immeasurable eons from now,
Born of the Okkāka clan,
he will be a teacher in the world known by the family name Gotama.
He is the heir to the Dhamma,
the legitimate son, fashioned by the Dhamma;
having fully understood all taints, he is free from them.
He will attain Nibbāna, free from taints;
having incinerated the defilements,
he will cross over the stream of craving.
"One named Bākula by name will become a disciple of the Teacher.
Having directly known all this,"
Gotama, the bull of the Sakyans,
having sat in the community of bhikkhus,
will place me at the very foremost.”
The Blessed One Anomadassī,
the self-become leader of the world,
gazing upon seclusion,
He approached me.
To the Great Hero who had arrived,
the Omniscient One, the Leader of the World;
With all kinds of medicine,
full of faith, I satisfied him with my own hands;
that well-performed deed of mine—
In a fertile field, there is an abundance of seed;
indeed, I am unable to exhaust it,
for my merit was well-performed at that time.
"Profit for me! Well-gained by me, that I have seen the Leader;
by the remainder of that karma,"
I have attained the immovable state.
Having directly known all this,
Gotama, the bull of the Sakyans;
Having sat within the community of bhikkhus,
he placed me in the foremost position.
In incalculable aeons from now,
Whatever deed I performed back then,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of that medicine.
The defilements have been incinerated by me;
all states of existence have been uprooted;
all taints are completely exhausted.
Now there is no further existence.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [as before] ...
The Buddha’s teaching has been proclaimed:
the four analytical knowledges, and so forth.
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, indeed, the venerable elder Bākula spoke these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the elder Bākula.
